text:
Maya (CEO): thanks everyone — we'll monitor this thread for follow-ups on the reorg/headcount decisions. short q's please.
Omar (Director, Eng): will managers get visibility into queued candidates for the roles that were paused?
Lila (Recruiter): yes, TA will publish a shared pipeline view. if your paused reqs have active candidates we'll highlight alternate fits and ask for manager preferences.
Ben (SRE): will the infra+platform hires be remote-friendly or mostly onsite? curious for hiring plans.
Priya (Head of People): most roles are remote-first but some site-sensitive roles (hardware ops, data center leads) will be expected onsite. location is in each JD.
Jonas (VP Eng): to be clear: priority = reliability, serving, and runtime. hiring velocity will be matched to impact metrics (SLO improvements, cost/unit).
Omar (Director, Eng): are managers allowed to re-allocate their hiring token mid-quarter if priorities change?
Priya (Head of People): yes, trade requests accepted — submit via the allocation sheet and mark as urgent if it affects launches. finance will review weekly.
Lila (Recruiter): process note: we're piloting a "panel share" approach — one candidate interview can be shared across two teams to speed hiring and reduce duplicate loops.
Ben (SRE): if a candidate is hired for team A but later moved to B within first 90 days, who owns onboarding?
Jonas (VP Eng): hiring team owns initial onboarding; receiving team owns role-specific ramp. we'll formalize 30/60/90 handoffs.
Maya (CEO): leadership office hours next Thurs 9am PT to go deeper. we'll post the final org map + a short FAQ by EOD tomorrow.
all-hands-bot: poll added "Do you feel supported to apply for internal moves?" options: Yes / Somewhat / No
Lila (Recruiter): follow-ups i'll post: 1) link to pipeline view, 2) allocation sheet, 3) internal mobility signup. please DM me for candidate introductions.
Maya (CEO): appreciate the questions — transparency is the priority. we'll keep this thread updated. :sparkles:
